thread:
Alex R.: spinning up eu-west4-gpu cluster and hitting bootstrapping failures — nodes stuck NotReady, GPU capacity 0/8 on new instances. ops-bot flagged BGP flaps earlier. logs attached below, cc @Priya S. @Mateo G.

Alex R.: ```
kubelet[1234]: E0901 10:12:03.123456    1234 server.go:XXXX] TLS handshake error from 10.0.2.5: remote error: tls: bad certificate
kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - module not loading
containerd: unable to start runtime: runtime network not ready: cni config: failed to add host route: write /proc/net/route: invalid argument
```

Priya S.: looks like two separate issues: kubelet certs (x509) and nvidia module mismatch. quick check — did the bootstrap use the new AMI?

Mateo G.: which AMI tag are we deploying? last time a kernel bump broke the nvidia module.

Alex R.: we're on `rwi-gpu-ami-2025-08` from image-service. kernel 6.2, but drivers in the AMI were built against 6.1. runtime logs show `nvidia: version magic 6.1` mismatch.

Jamie L.: if drivers don't load the k8s device plugin reports 0 GPUs -> kubelet marks capacity. suggestion: rollback launch-template to `rwi-gpu-ami-2025-07` and spin a few nodes for validation. also we saw CNI route errors — could be MTU mismatch with peering.

Priya S.: agreed. steps to mitigate:
1) patch ASG launch template to previous AMI
2) cordon + drain failing nodes (they're not serving anyway)
3) update CNI MTU to 8900 if peering supports jumbo frames

Priya S.: commands:
```bash
# update launch template (example)
aws ec2 modify-launch-template --launch-template-id lt-0abcd --default-version 12
# cordon/drain
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-2-5.eu-west4.internal
kubectl drain ip-10-0-2-5.eu-west4.internal --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```

ops-bot: INCIDENT created: inc-2025-1883 | severity:p2 | region: eu-west4 | owner: @eng-infra-oncall

deploy-bot: triggered rolling-update for asg eu-west4-gpu-pool -> using `rwi-gpu-ami-2025-07`

Alex R.: after switching the LT, new instances booted and drivers loaded on 3/3 new nodes. kubectl shows GPU allocatable back to expected. however autoscaler still not scaling down/up: ASG tags + taints mismatch. nodes are tainted `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule` and our test workloads don't have tolerations.

Mateo G.: also saw intermittent BGP flap messages in the fabric logs — reported to cloud-net support. they pointed at MTU mismatch on the transit link. I pushed CNI MTU 8900 to the daemonset config and restarted pods on the new nodes.

Jamie L.: on the cost side, this pool was mostly spot. two spot terminations coincided with bootstrap failures — we should keep at least 10% on-demand for critical GPU pools during handoffs. ops playbook update? :thinking_face:

Priya S.: noted. I'll add a short playbook line in the runbook: retain 1-2 on-demand instances until QA signoff.

Alex R.: current status:
- AMI rolled back to `rwi-gpu-ami-2025-07` (done)
- CNI MTU patched to 8900 (done)
- New nodes joined and registered GPU allocatable 8/8 on each (validated)
- Autoscaler fix: added nodegroup tag `k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled=true` and updated test job tolerations (done)

Mateo G.: quick validations ran: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` shows Ready, `kubectl describe node` shows `nvidia.com/gpu: 8 allocatable`. e2e smoke suite passed against the cluster (basic ml-serving). :thumbsup:

ops-bot: inc-2025-1883 updated: status -> mitigation in progress; assigned -> eng-infra-oncall.

Jamie L.: handing off to oncall for long tail checks and dashboard monitoring. @eng-oncall please verify metrics: pod_scheduling_latency, node_gpu_allocatable, BGP route stability, and alert on flaps.

Priya S.: oncall handoff: we've completed rollback and MTU fix; please watch for recurrence for 2 hours and escalate if BGP flaps resume. Link to runbook snippet: https://internal/docs/runbooks/eu-west4-gpu-bootstrap (private).

Alex R.: final note — we'll bake a new AMI with drivers for kernel 6.2 and run a canary pool next week. for now closing thread when oncall confirms stability. :white_check_mark:
